The individual quote tests pass, but the deployed Courier CLI sometimes picks ground for priority parcels, sends hazardous freight by air, and keeps yesterday's carrier prices. Operators call this flaky; reproduce the deterministic order dependence and fix the underlying planning/caching behavior, not the symptoms in the CLI. Equal-priority routes must use lexicographic code order, and registry registration/replacement/removal must be visible on the very next call even after a cached miss. Country normalization, eligibility for all request fields, errors, response fields and arithmetic must remain as documented.
Add regression tests covering mixed request order, warmed services, and registry changes; update the README with a brief explanation of the corrected caching strategy. Do not remove caching by rebuilding an entire service or re-importing plugins per request.
